questions.question: What is the difference between `systemctl start myapp` and `systemctl enable myapp`?
options: start runs it now; enable makes it start at boot
enable runs it now; start makes it start at boot
start runs it as root; enable runs it as the current user
questions.explanation: start affects the running system immediately; enable only affects future boots. systemctl enable --now does both.

questions.question: You edited `/etc/systemd/system/myapp.service` and restarted the service, but your change had no effect. What did you most likely forget?
questions.explanation: systemd caches unit files. After creating or editing one, run sudo systemctl daemon-reload so it re-reads them.

questions.question: Which statement about `ExecStart=` in a service unit is correct?
options: It runs through Bash, so pipes and && work
It accepts a relative path resolved against WorkingDirectory
It is optional for Type=simple services
It needs an absolute path and is not run through a shell, so pipes and ~ do not work
questions.explanation: systemd executes the command directly rather than via a shell. Put complex logic in a script and point ExecStart at it.

questions.question: Which command follows the live logs of the `myapp` service?
questions.explanation: -u filters by unit and -f follows new entries, like tail -f. -p filters by priority, not unit.
